title: Perf run 20261018-1719
heading: Fixes, checks and two small removals, with no player moment slower: the computer's games and the tutorial now open no connection to the server
meta:
This general run kept 18 changes, each held to the skill's bar of evidence: 7 fixes (one of them to the bench, at grading), 1 visibility fix, 8 new checks and 2 small removals. A third removal, CK1, was reverted at grading because the row it touches leaned slower twice; it waits in the ledger with its patch. It claims no speed change. The most visible fix: a game against the computer and the tutorial no longer connect to the game server, so they no longer wake its container or hold an idle connection.

The final A/B ran the branch (05b74df) against the base 9a9e9db, all 16 headline rows, 8 interleaved pairs. No row was called better or worse. Nine rows leaned slower at the median pair. A second A/B of the five game rows among them, 8 pairs, showed none of those leans again. The other four leans are listed under Needs from me, as information.

needs.intro: Nothing here needs a decision. The first two items are trade-offs this run's fixes make, named so they can be weighed; the rest is information, with a recommendation.

items.title: Trade-off: the computer answers an offer at once, but its next reply after a dropped thought starts a new worker (1015:CC, 13a488c)
items.body: Before, a draw offer or a take-back during the computer's search waited behind that search, up to 1.8 s. Now the dropped thought ends its worker and the answer comes at once. The cost: the computer's next reply has to start a new search worker, which loads its chunk and builds its tables, about 3.3 MB. That cost is not measured.
items.recommend: Keep it. The next speed run measures that reply against an ordinary one (ledger CC2); if it shows, build the replacement worker at dispose time or when idle.

items.title: Trade-off: the computer's pages and the tutorial no longer open the server connection (1014:ES, 0dcd5bb, 6716adc)
items.body: /computer, /computer/:id and /learn no longer connect to the game server, so they no longer wake it or hold an idle connection. The cost: a player who goes from one of those pages to /new now connects there cold, where before the connection was already open.
items.recommend: Keep it. If /new's first screen leans slower from those pages, connect when the player heads for Play a friend.

items.title: Information: four headline rows leaned slower in the final A/B and were not measured again
items.body:
The skill's speed rule lists any headline row that is more than 3% worse at its median pair. In the final A/B (8 pairs, nothing called) nine rows did. The five game rows among them were measured again, 8 more pairs: none was more than 3% worse (ab-20261018-1719-recheck.md), so those leans came from the machine. The other four, with their pairs (head/base):

  • Start page shows the board, desktop: ×1.073 at the median pair, 5 of 8 worse (1.09 1.18 0.91 1.08 1.15 0.89 1.06 0.98). The DL1 row: this row swings on identical code.
  • Start page answers its first click, desktop: 15.3 → 15.7 ms, ×1.151 at the median pair, 5 of 8 worse (0.85 1.37 1.16 0.73 1.14 1.17 1.19 0.91). CK1 touched this click, and run 2100's A/B of CK1 leaned the same way (×1.114, 5 of 8). The change is 0.4 ms, but speed ranks above less code, so CK1 was reverted at grading (ddfa59f): the start page's code is the base's again. The row was not measured after the revert.
  • First board picture, playing the computer: 1.39 → 1.45 s, ×1.113, 6 of 8 worse (1.00 1.25 1.09 1.18 1.14 1.15 0.84 0.93). The run's change on that path removes a socket; it adds no work.
  • Reopening a long game: ×1.198, 4 of 8 worse (0.79 1.79 2.02 0.77 1.60 0.41 0.35 1.67). The run changed no code on that path.
items.recommend: No action. The next speed run takes the desktop rows with DL1 and FC1 (a 16-pair A/A of the desktop rows first), and can include the computer's section in its first A/B.

Against the first recorded run the branch is 2.41 times as fast over 13 rows (the long view, below).

items.title: The branch against the base
items.body: 05b74df against 9a9e9db, all 16 headline rows, 8 interleaved pairs: ×0.942 over the 16 rows, 0 called better, 0 called worse, and 0 of the 110 diagnostics called. The re-check of the five game rows, 8 pairs, gave ×1.035 over those rows, none more than 3% worse. The commits after 05b74df: ddfa59f reverts CK1, so StartScreen.tsx is the base's bytes again; a142c36 is a test fix; 8a3e922 is the bench's preview server, used by both sides; then the merge of main (25c27f9, #166) and the withdrawal of a test it made stale (b2fc83a); the rest are bench/loop/. No re-measure is needed: the CK1 revert returns that code to the base, and the rest are tests and bench.

items.title: The long view: against the first recorded run
items.body: Measured at grading: 8a3e922 (its app code is a142c36's, the PR's) against the first recorded run's base 92ce041, --primary, 3 interleaved pairs (ab-20261018-1719-vs-first-run.md). Over the 13 headline rows both sides can measure, the head is 2.41 times as fast (run 20261016-0037 measured 2.48 on 11 rows). 7 rows are called better: the moves and the pick-up (about 0.2–0.3 s against about 3 s), the board on the start page (desktop −60%, phone −72%, a returning phone −73%) and a returning phone's start page usable (−24%). One is called worse, as in run 0037: the phone's start page usable, 601 → 680 ms (+11%, 3 of 3 pairs; +13% then), since the start page has grown (the computer player, the tutorial, the picture). Not called but over 3% worse: the desktop first click 9.4 → 11.6 ms (2 of 3 pairs) and the joiner's first board picture +4.9% (2 of 3). The base has no computer player or review, so three rows are missing on its side. The bench could serve this base again only after 8a3e922.

changed.intro: Each change below has its own commit, and its evidence is in that commit's message. A fix has a test that fails on the base and passes on the branch. A new check was broken once on purpose to show that it fails.

items.title: No connection to the server from the computer's pages and the tutorial (1014:ES: 0dcd5bb, 6716adc, a142c36)
items.body:
Before, the built page's inline script opened a socket to the game server on every page, and the app opened its own one where the script had not. A game against the computer and the tutorial never send anything to the server, yet they woke its container and held the connection open. 0dcd5bb stopped the inline script on those pages. The review found that the app's socket still opened there, so 6716adc makes the app's socket wait for a page that uses the server: it opens on the way to /new. A new test renders the app at /computer, /computer/abc123 and /learn and finds no socket, then one after moving to /new. It fails on 0dcd5bb. The commit message of 0dcd5bb claims the whole fix; 6716adc completes it.

At grading, CI's client check failed on the new navigation test: on /learn the tutorial's lazy canvas could arrive during the test's wait and mount the real scene under the test's stand-in for three.js. a142c36 stubs that canvas, as the test already stubs the start page's preview; the whole suite passes (124 files, 1,475 tests).

Its trade-off is under Needs from me.

items.title: A double tap sends a request to the opponent once (online half of 1015:I13, 8eedbfb)
items.body: A second tap on Resign, Draw, Take back or Rematch within the server's round trip sent the request twice, and the server's refusal stayed on screen as an error. Each request now goes once until a message arrives.

items.title: Escape closes the result card and the promotion picker after a click on them (Escape half of 1015:I15, ec4d60a)
items.body: A click on the card's words moved focus to the page, so Escape did nothing. The two cards now take focus on a click. Before/after screenshots in Chromium at 390×844 and 1280×800, after a click on each card's heading: before, the focus went to the page and Escape left the card open; after, the focus is on the card, it matches no :focus-visible, no ring is drawn, and Escape closes it. WebKit and Firefox are not installed on the run's machine and were not checked (ledger I15).

items.title: The computer's worker: freed when its thought is dropped, and a warning when it cannot start (1015:CC, 13a488c; 182e2b0)
items.body:
A thought dropped before its answer (a draw offer or a take-back during the computer's search) kept its worker busy, and the next question waited behind it. The dropped thought now ends its worker and the next question gets a fresh one. Separately, when new Worker throws, the computer now says so in the console instead of falling back silently.

Its trade-off is under Needs from me.

items.title: The start page's early picture keeps the cut the head preloaded (1018-0317:EP1, 58b88eb)
items.body: The page's head preloads one cut of the board's picture and its body then chose again, so on some window heights it fetched a second cut. The body now keeps the preloaded cut while it still covers the window.

items.title: The A/B's calling rule: from 10 pairs on, the lowest and highest ratio are left out of the spread (1017-1252:VR1, d85cade)
items.body: One far pair blocked a call that every pair agreed on. Every pair must still move the same way. Flipping the signs of every committed report's pairs at random gives 0.022 chance calls expected over the 373 rows with 10 or more pairs, against 0.009 under the old rule. An A/A of the client tier, 12 pairs, called 0 of 120 rows (ab-20261018-1719-aa-client.md).

items.title: The bench serves a build with no _headers, so the long view runs again (8a3e922)
items.body: Fix, found at grading. Since fbac15f the browser bench's header plugin read the build's _headers unconditionally. The first recorded run's base, 92ce041, predates that file, so its preview server failed to start and an A/B against it measured only the head. Such a build is now served with no headers, as its host served it. Evidence: the preview config test now also removes the file and expects no headers; it fails on the old plugin and passes here. The long view below was measured with it.

items.title: New checks (f9ee5ca, d9108c2, d9796ab, 900ef97, 57f77dd, 7ae1e19)
items.body:
• public/landing holds only the pictures the page asks for, and the entry's __LANDING_VERSION__ define is checked.
  • og.jpg's size and format are compared with the page's link-preview tags. (The same commit pinned the HUD's piece values to the computer's; that pin was withdrawn after #166 made them differ on purpose.)
  • A layout's start page pictures share one pixel density.
  • The bench's preview server reads the build's own _headers.
  • Every part of a headline row's name is written in its bench.
  • eslint.config.test.mjs lints one line per CLAUDE.md lint rule in each part of the code.

removed.intro:
• Six GameScreen test files stub the lazily loaded board once instead of nine three.js modules each (part of D10, be7492c). Screens layer, tests only: 19 lines in, 112 out. Duplication in the six files (jscpd, 5 lines or 50 tokens): 7 clones, 100 lines (8.95%) → 3 clones, 21 lines (2.05%). Complexity (ESLint's complexity): 280 functions summing 298 → 184 summing 194; the largest is 3 before and after.
  • The move record draws and says a move through one small component instead of two copies of the same markup (MH2, dd7eead). Screens layer, app: 22 lines in, 21 out. Duplication in MoveHistory.tsx (jscpd, 2 lines or 20 tokens): 1 clone of 3 lines → none. Complexity: 29 functions summing 149, largest 59 → 30 summing 150, largest 58.
  • CK1 (the start page click's flushSync, 986e325) was removed and then restored at grading (ddfa59f), so it removes nothing. Its patch is back in bench/loop/patches/.

Lines per layer over the run (9a9e9db..8a3e922, outside bench/loop/; app, then tests): screens +55 −32 and +87 −113; hooks and lib +25 −3 and +47 −1; ai +3 −1 and +16 −0; game +1 −1 and +20 −1; three, tests only, +21 −2; bench +20 −5 and +55 −4; other (index.html, config, and the config and lint tests) +3 −1 and +126 −0. The engine and the server are untouched. In the whole screens folder, duplication fell from 18 clones, 212 lines (1.47%) to 13 clones, 118 lines (0.82%), and the complexity sum from 2,247 to 2,161 (largest 88 both). The run mostly added checks, so the code grew.

items.title: CK1: the start page click without flushSync (reverted, parked)
items.body: Kept in Improve as a removal with no speed claim, then reverted at grading (ddfa59f): the desktop first click leaned slower in both of its A/Bs (run 2100 ×1.114 and this run's final ×1.151, 5 of 8 pairs each, neither called). It waits first in the ledger with its patch for an A/B of the start page section with 16 or more pairs.

items.title: M9: one set of search tables per thread (not landed, parked for the speed run)
items.body: A/B against 986e325, the computer's search, 12 pairs: “The computer's strength in its time” 50.1 → 29.7 ms at the median pair, 11 of 12 pairs below 1 and one at 1.17, so not called (ab-20261018-1719-m9.md). Not a rejection: it is the first item for the next speed run, with its patch, 16 or more pairs and a probe of its idle memory.

items.title: RW1: the review on every core
items.body: Closed without measuring. Its fourth worker takes the page's own core, which lengthens the longest freeze during the review: a trade between two player moments.

items.title: CK2(c): a stricter check of the start page pictures' cover
items.body: An existing test already fails on the same break, so the new one added nothing.

choices.intro:
• Fixed ES's review blocker in the code (the app's socket waits for a page that uses the server) instead of rewording the claim. A page that goes from /new to /computer now closes its socket and opens a fresh one on the way back.
  • Ran the final A/B at 8 pairs, then re-ran the five game rows that leaned, 8 pairs, instead of every section again. The four rows not re-run are listed under Needs from me.
  • VR1 trims from 10 pairs, not 8: from 8 the chance calls on the committed reports grow about five-fold.
  • I13's latch is per request type, so a draw offer and a take-back in one round trip both go.
  • Parked six ledger rows that three runs passed over (CG1, HW1, SV1, AV1, RF1, BS1).
  • At grading, reverted CK1 rather than measure it again: an A/B of the start page with enough pairs to clear a 0.4 ms lean would not fit the stage. Speed ranks above less code.
  • At grading, moved M9 back to the top of the ledger's Open list for the speed run instead of closing it.
  • At grading, fixed the bench (it could not serve a build without _headers) and measured the long view, rather than leave it to the next run.

notConfirmed.intro:
• The four leaning rows above were not measured again, nor the desktop first click after CK1's revert.
  • Whether a key pressed after a click on the result card makes Chromium, Firefox or WebKit draw a focus ring round it (ledger I15).
  • The cost of the fresh worker after a dropped thought (ledger CC2).
  • DL1's per-load desktop figures: read from raw output that is not committed, so they stay a lead.
  • Why programs.spec.ts's review test failed once in the full e2e run on ddfa59f; it passed when run alone (ledger PG1).

  2. PG1: e2e/programs.spec.ts's review test failed once in a full e2e run on ddfa59f (three marks' programs linked after the warm-up) and passed alone.
